question_text: A bag contains 1 blue ticket, 3 red tickets, and 8 yellow tickets. A player randomly selects a ticket from the bag, and receives $40 for a blue ticket, $20 for a red ticket, and $5 for a yellow ticket.

subparts.stem: Calculate the expected return for one trial of this game.
subparts.solution:
Let $X$ be the return from each game.
$$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|} \hline \text{Ticket colour} & \text{Blue} & \text{Red} & \text{Yellow} \\ \hline \text{Winnings} & \$40 & \$20 & \$5 \\ \hline \text{Probability} & \frac{1}{12} & \frac{3}{12} & \frac{8}{12} \\ \hline \end{array}$$

$\begin{aligned} E(X) &= 40\left(\frac{1}{12}\right) + 20\left(\frac{3}{12}\right) + 5\left(\frac{8}{12}\right) \\ &= \frac{40 + 60 + 40}{12} \\ &= \frac{140}{12} \\ &\approx \$11.67 \end{aligned}$

ai_explanation.concept_rule: The expected return is the sum of the product of each payout and its probability.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Subtracting the ticket cost prematurely when asked for the expected return.

subparts.stem: Given that the game costs $15 to play, explain why it would not be advisable to play this game.

mark_breakdown.desc: Compute net gain: expected return minus cost
Conclude that playing is not advisable due to negative expected gain

subparts.solution:
The expected return per game is $\$11.67$. It costs $\$15$ to play.
So, the expected gain $\approx \$11.67 - \$15 \approx -\$3.33$.
It is not advisable to play this game many times as the player can expect to lose $\$3.33$ on average per game.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: A game is favorable if expected net gain $> 0$, fair if $= 0$, and unfavorable if $< 0$.
step_by_step: Since expected gain is negative, it is not advisable to play repeatedly.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Neglecting to provide a clear concluding recommendation.

subparts.stem: Find the number of extra red tickets that should be added to the bag to make the game fair.

mark_breakdown.desc: Express new probabilities in terms of $k$ extra red tickets
Set expected return equal to game cost of $\$15$

subparts.solution:
Let $k$ be the number of extra red tickets added to the bag.
$$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|} \hline \text{Ticket colour} & \text{Blue} & \text{Red} & \text{Yellow} \\ \hline \text{Winnings} & \$40 & \$20 & \$5 \\ \hline \text{Probability} & \frac{1}{12+k} & \frac{k+3}{12+k} & \frac{8}{12+k} \\ \hline \end{array}$$

For the game to be fair, the expected return must equal the cost of each game.
$\begin{aligned} \therefore E(X) = 40\left(\frac{1}{12+k}\right) + 20\left(\frac{k+3}{12+k}\right) + 5\left(\frac{8}{12+k}\right) &= 15 \\ \frac{40}{12+k} + \frac{20k + 60}{12+k} + \frac{40}{12+k} &= 15 \\ \frac{20k + 140}{12+k} &= 15 \\ 20k + 140 &= 15(12+k) \\ 20k + 140 &= 180 + 15k \\ 5k &= 40 \\ k &= 8 \end{aligned}$

So, 8 extra red tickets should be added to the bag to make the game fair.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: A game is fair when the expected return equals the cost to play ($E(X) = 15$).
step_by_step: With $k$ red tickets added, total tickets become $12+k$, and red tickets become $3+k$.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Forgetting to update the denominator to $12+k$ for all ticket types.
